claim: Analogy projects unmatched base facts connected to the matched structure as candidate inferences, and these are guesses that can be false (SME output included a false 'solid alcohol' and an invented skolem entity).
agent_test: Have the agent list transferred steps explicitly as 'candidates' and log how many fail the later test.

claim: Candidate inference has three states: proposed, usable (no contradiction, no unknown objects), adopted (survived testing). Testing after transfer is a separate step.
agent_test: Compare transfer-then-test against transfer-and-trust at equal tokens; count wrong adopted steps.

claim: People project inferences along connected causal structure: with an analogy they predict the shared-system base fact about 53% vs 12% without (Exp 2, N=32); replicated in Exp 3 (N=48).
agent_test: Prefer carrying steps that sit inside the shared causal chain; check by ablating isolated-fact transfers.

claim: Comparing two cases beats studying them separately for transfer (48% vs 19%, N=128; negotiation contracts 90% vs 55%). Meta-analytic d~0.5 is from memory only.
agent_test: Give the agent two aligned solved cases vs one at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Gap search: the early meta-analysis abstract (opened) gives d=.60, CI .47-.72, 57 experiments; the final paper's d=.50 is from a snippet only. Quote 'medium, about .5 to .6'. No LLM test of two aligned sources found; Yasunaga K=1 vs K>=3 (76.1 vs 77.5 GSM8K) is only indirect.

claim: Spontaneous analogue use is rare and a hint raises it (29% to 50% in Gick and Holyoak 1983; HR problem 37% vs 20% in 2025 sample). The original 1980 numbers were not opened.
agent_test: Check whether a prompt cue to 'use earlier cases' raises correct transfer.
gap_search_note: Gap search: Gick and Holyoak 1983 Exp 2 rates 29% (8/28) and 50% (14/28) confirmed via a 2025 replication paper's quote (opened). 1980 numbers still unread. A 2025 GPT-4 run used the wrong source about half the time when hinted.

claim: Frontier LLMs retrieve structurally matching sources well in near cases but fail on far analogies (GPT-4 39.6% vs humans 94.1% on ARN far; ChatGPT ~30% on StoryAnalogy MC; GPT-3 far story p=0.065).
agent_test: Test source selection with surface-similar distractors at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Gap search: ARN table read. The 39.6 is the all-model mean of the two far cells (45.3 and 33.9); GPT-4 alone is 57.1 and 29.1. 2026 frontier models (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.5) reach MAP about 0.82 on ARN ranking, but the far-with-near-distractor cell was not isolated, so persistence in frontier models is not settled.

claim: Matching, not recall, is the weak step: GPT-4 recalls nearly all relevant analogies but applies wrong ones often.
agent_test: Add a mapping-check step before transferring a step and measure wrong-transfer rate.

claim: LLM letter-string analogy success is brittle under counterfactual alphabets (humans .753; GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452) and near-zero for GPT-3 on synthetic alphabets (<0.1).
schema_part: G (do not trust analogical success on familiar surface forms)
agent_test: Run counterfactual variants of the agent's own analogy tasks.

claim: The brittleness may be mechanical (counting), not lack of abstraction: GPT-4 with code execution matched humans (P=0.496); 46% of its errors used a valid alternative rule.
agent_test: Compare agent with and without code tool on permuted-structure analogies.

claim: Models are order- and paraphrase-sensitive on story analogies and over-trust a misleading source (GPT-4 0.89 first vs 0.61 second position; Random Finals falls 0.8 vs humans 0.5).
agent_test: Randomise source order and inject a misleading source; measure drop.
gap_search_note: Gap search: GPT-4 order bias re-read (0.89/0.61 first/second in Webb data; 1.0/0.72 in Lewis and Mitchell run; humans 0.78/0.78). Reasoning-trained models were not tested in anything opened. o3-mini and R1 fall from 86.6/80.6 to 17.0/23.2 on I-RAVEN-X, so brittleness likely persists but for a different task.

claim: Self-generated analogical exemplars give modest gains (+4% avg; GSM8K 76.7 to 77.8 GPT-3.5; Codeforces Acc@1 13 to 15%) and only help big models; small models prefer retrieved exemplars.
agent_test: Replicate at equal tokens against 3-shot CoT.
gap_search_note: Gap search: K=1 exemplar is worst, K=3 to 5 plateau (GSM8K 76.1 to 77.8). Manual check of 100 runs: 21 had relevant exemplars with wrong solutions.

claim: The relevance explanation for self-generated analogies is refuted on maths: irrelevant or random self-generated examples did as well or better (relevant 71.5/33.3 vs N/A 75.5/36.1 GSM8K/MATH, GPT-3.5); accuracy of examples (62% vs 72% vs 86%) drives scores.
schema_part: O7: do not credit 'analogy' for gains
agent_test: Run relevant vs random self-generated exemplars on the agent.
gap_search_note: Gap search: MATH label confirmed (Table 5: example accuracy relevant 62%, N/A 72%, random-same 86%, n=50 each). Holds on GSM8K for GPT-4o-mini (90.7 relevant vs 93.2 random-bio) but relevance wins on BBH (63.2 vs 61.9). Task-dependent; not tested on reasoning models.

claim: Solving analogous problems and reusing their results improves optimal-path rate (GPT-3.5 0.33 to 0.65; GPT-4 0.78 to 0.88) and ALFWorld completion; costs several extra calls.
agent_test: Match token budget against best-of-N.
gap_search_note: Gap search: re-checked. GPT-3.5 0-shot OR 0.33 to 0.65, GPT-4 0.78 to 0.88; still single-source, no replication.

claim: Text re-encoding of relational structure lets LLMs beat humans on Raven-style tasks (GPT-3 Center 77.2%; 3x3 grid 93.2% with decomposition), so explicit structure aids inference.
agent_test: Compare free-form vs structured relation listing before transfer.

claim: Adding an explicit structure-mapping engine over LLM abstractions lifts below-chance mapping to 0.46 (chance 0.25); LLM-only best 0.41.
agent_test: Use code-side one-to-one mapping check on the agent's analogies.
gap_search_note: Gap search: Table 3 read from text: MCQ Qwen 0.41 to 0.46, Llama 0.28 to 0.45; ARN far Qwen 0.47 vs zero-shot 0.52 (worse), Llama 0.46 vs 0.42 (better). 8B models, picks stories, not steps; no matched compute. Narrow to 'helps weak models on some splits'.

claim: Cross-domain analogy prompting raises solution novelty (Claude 1.6% to 50.4%; model rows partly inferred) but novelty is not validity.
agent_test: Pair novelty gain with a correctness check.
gap_search_note: Gap search: human check found AR more novel 78% of 50 pairs (kappa .445) but judged reasonable only 67% vs 86% for the cross-domain baseline (kappa .155 vs .416); raters saw the source domain, four raters, not a blind correctness test. Per-model novelty numbers now read: Claude 1.28/3.12/5.54, GPT 1.98/3.69/6.14, Gemini 2.11/4.68/6.43.

claim: Gap: no study was found that measures LLM projection of unmatched base facts as candidate inferences and their correctness rate directly.
agent_test: Build a small benchmark: provide base+target, score each carried-over step true/false.
gap_search_note: Gap search: still true. Closest proxies: wrong-source rate ~50% when hinted (d16), 21/100 runs with wrong self-made exemplar (d04). No test-before-adopt arm, no one-vs-two-source LLM test, no skolem-repair probe found; quota ran out.

claim: Self-made sources are wrong often enough to need a check: about 21 of 100 hand-checked runs carried a relevant exemplar with an incorrect solution (GPT-3.5), and GPT-4 given a hint applied the wrong analogue about half the time (precision 0.50 to 0.52, n=15 per cell).
agent_test: Run O7 with and without a test-before-adopt step at equal tokens; count adopted steps later found false.

claim: The ARN far-analogy collapse is a surface-vs-structure choice problem: the 39.6% figure is the mean of far-vs-far (45.3) and far-vs-near-distractor (33.9) over all models; GPT-4 scored 57.1 and 29.1. A 2026 ranking test on ARN gives GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.5 MAP about 0.82, so frontier persistence is unresolved.
agent_test: Test frontier and reasoning models on the far-analogy-with-near-distractor cell with order shuffled.

claim: Analogy-guided far-domain generation trades correctness for novelty: AR was judged more novel in 78% of 50 pairs but reasonable only 67% vs 86% for the cross-domain baseline.
agent_test: After far-domain transfer, require an executable or logical test before adoption and log pass rate.

claim: Reasoning models are not immune to analogy brittleness: o3-mini fell from 86.6% to 17.0% and DeepSeek R1 from 80.6% to 23.2% on I-RAVEN-X, while a symbolic neuro-symbolic solver held 88.0%; more reasoning tokens did not help.
agent_test: Compare code-side one-to-one mapping against free reasoning at matched tokens on a held-out analogy set.
